title: GRASP: Differentially Private Graph Reconstruction Defense with Structured Perturbation

problem.claim: Existing differentially private graph neural networks are ineffective against graph reconstruction attacks.

gap.claim: Existing perturbation mechanisms induce an unidirectional shift in embedding similarities without sufficiently disrupting their relative ranking, allowing graph reconstruction attacks to recover the original graph structure.

contributions.claim: GRASP is a differentially private graph neural network based on structured perturbation.
GRASP integrates independent and identical noise through a Bernoulli technique to promote bidirectional shifts in embedding similarity and disrupt relative ranking.
The implementation of GRASP is publicly available.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GRASP as a novel differentially private graph neural network based on structured perturbation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that GRASP effectively defends against graph reconstruction attacks.
GRASP achieves a superior privacy-utility trade-off compared with existing graph structure protection methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing differentially private graph neural networks are ineffective against graph reconstruction attacks.
The ineffectiveness is attributed to unstructured perturbation that shifts embedding similarities in one direction while preserving relative ranking.
GRASP introduces structured perturbation by combining independent and identical noise with a Bernoulli technique.
The authors report effective defense against graph reconstruction attacks on eight benchmark datasets and a superior privacy-utility trade-off.
The implementation is reported as available online.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the threat model, privacy budget, or attack and defense configurations.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, dataset names, baselines, or statistical comparisons.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the Bernoulli technique or structured perturbation mechanism.
